title: Actual semi-invariant section modules and rational left translation
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $G,B$ be $F$-group schemes with homomorphism $i:B\to G$ [def-sc-group-scheme]. Write $F[G]=\Gamma(G,\mathcal O_G)$ with its scalar structure from $G\to\operatorname{Spec}F$. For every commutative $F$-algebra $A$ and $g:\operatorname{Spec}A\to G$, evaluation $\operatorname{ev}_g:F[G]\to A$ is pullback on global sections, followed by $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A,\mathcal O)=A$. For a character $\chi:B\to\mathbf G_m$ [def-sc-gm-ga] and $m\in\mathbf N$, define the actual submodule $W(G,B,i,\chi,m)\subseteq F[G]$ by the equations $\operatorname{ev}_{g i(b)}(f)=\chi(b)^m\operatorname{ev}_g(f)$ for every $A$, $g\in G(A)$ and $b\in B(A)$. Equivalently this is the intersection of the kernels of those $F$-linear difference maps. For a finite-dimensional subspace $W\subseteq F[G]$, say that $W$ has rational left translation if there are a finite index set $I$, an $F$-linear isomorphism $e:F^I\simeq W$, and an algebraic-group representation $r:G\to\operatorname{GL}_I$ in the sense of [def-wf-algebraic-representations], such that, writing $f_j=e(\delta_j)$, one has $\sum_i r(s)_{ij}\operatorname{ev}_g(f_i)=\operatorname{ev}_{s^{-1}g}(f_j)$ for every commutative $F$-algebra $A$, $s,g\in G(A)$ and $j\in I$. This specifies the action on the actual functions; the basis merely expresses the rational action on this subspace in coordinates. The zero-dimensional case is included.
